Question Choices: Select. Two triangles share side PQ. Which property justifies PQ = PQ? ~~Reflexive property | Symmetric property | Transitive property~~
Hints: A quantity always equals itself.|The shared side is the same segment in both triangles.
Solution: The segment PQ is the very same segment in both triangles. The reflexive property gives PQ = PQ; equivalently, the segment is congruent to itself.

Question Choices: Select. Two intersecting lines create a pair of vertical angles. Why are those angles congruent? ~~Pythagorean theorem | Vertical angles theorem | Triangle angle-sum theorem~~
Hints: They lie opposite each other at the intersection.|Both are supplementary to the same angle.
Solution: Vertical angles lie opposite at the intersection. Each is supplementary to the same adjacent angle. Subtracting that common angle from 180 degrees gives equal measures, so vertical angles are congruent.

Question Choices: Select. Point M is the midpoint of XY. What relationship follows? ~~XM = XY | MY = XY | XM = MY~~
Hints: A midpoint divides a segment into two equal parts.|Name the subsegments on each side of M.
Solution: A midpoint lies on the segment and divides it into two equal lengths. By definition, XM = MY.

Question Choices: Select. Two lines are perpendicular. What type of angles do they form? ~~Obtuse angles | Right angles | Acute angles~~
Hints: Perpendicular means meeting at 90 degrees.|All four angles at the intersection are equal.
Solution: By definition, perpendicular lines meet at right angles. Each of the four angles at the intersection is 90 degrees.

Question Choices: Select. Ray BD bisects angle ABC. What relationship follows? ~~Angle DBC = angle ABC | Angle ABD = angle DBC | Angle ABD = angle ABC~~
Hints: An angle bisector splits an angle into two equal parts.|Name the two smaller angles.
Solution: An angle bisector divides an angle into two equal angles at the same vertex. Ray BD divides angle ABC into angles ABD and DBC, so those angles are congruent.
